items.title: PlanCompileRun storage identity is explicit
items.statement: The registry materializes a launch-critical redb family keyed by project and run identifiers, with an explicit value schema and owner document.

items.title: PlanCompileRun replay is fail-closed
items.statement: Resume targets an exact run id, while stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.title: PlanCompileRun consumers are enumerated
items.statement: The stored run feeds exact-id resume/restart, Planning Wizard disabled-state projection, and the implementation-readiness gate.

items.title: Compiler wave storage boundary is explicit
items.statement: The compiler-wave row is keyed by project, compile run, and assignment and requires read, write, forbidden-write, parent-only-write, receipt, retry, evidence, and writeback fields.

items.title: Compiler wave replay excludes product work
items.statement: Replay restores assignment state and parent-only write obligations without dispatching product work.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay restores assignment state and parent-only write obligations without dispatching product work.",

items.title: Currentness and cursor have no value contract
items.statement: The fail-closed replay rule depends on stale currentness, but cursor and currentness_status are unconstrained objects. The row therefore cannot be implemented or validated consistently for staleness, cursor position, or resume eligibility from this contract.
items.impact: Different builders can encode and interpret currentness and cursor incompatibly, causing divergent enable/disable and resume outcomes.
items.builder_discretion: Object members, required keys, status vocabulary, freshness basis, cursor semantics, and validation rules are all left open.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.title: Run status and stage transitions are unspecified
items.statement: The schema enumerates run statuses but accepts any non-empty current_stage and defines no legal transition graph, terminality rule, status-stage invariant, or transition authority.
items.impact: Resume, cancellation, supersession, and readiness projections can disagree about whether a stored run is legal or terminal.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent stage names, allowed transitions, guards, and the mapping between stage and status.

items.title: Receipt completeness cannot be determined
items.statement: Receipts are required but may be an empty array of arbitrary strings. The contract never defines which receipts are required at each stage, their identity or integrity, or the exact meaning of missing receipts used by the disable rule.
items.impact: Implementations cannot deterministically decide whether PlanCompile must remain disabled or whether evidence is complete.
items.builder_discretion: Receipt taxonomy, minimum set, stage mapping, reference syntax, hash binding, and completeness predicate are open.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.title: PNC-019 enablement transition is absent
items.statement: The only runtime_adapter value is disabled_until_pnc019 and the family remains blocked by PNC-019, while runtime enablement and policy references are nullable arbitrary strings. No transition, authority, validation, or migration rule explains how runtime becomes enabled.
items.impact: A builder cannot safely lift the runtime-disabled state or validate that an enablement reference authorizes execution.
items.builder_discretion: Enablement state, trigger, signer or authority, required policy snapshot, adapter migration, and rollback are undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical Tier 0C-2 PlanCompileRun storage contract, still blocked by PNC-019 runtime lifecycle.",

items.title: Key identity is not bound to payload identity
items.statement: Both key shapes embed identifiers that also appear in the value, but the schemas only require non-empty strings and state no equality invariant between key segments and payload fields.
items.impact: A row can be stored under one project, run, or assignment key while claiming another identity in its payload, breaking replay and ownership isolation.
items.builder_discretion: Key parsing, normalization, equality checks, and rejection behavior are unspecified.

items.title: Nested run metadata remains opaque
items.statement: source_hashes, cancellation, and supersession are unrestricted objects, so provenance, cancellation authority, causal linkage, and supersession ordering are not contractual.
items.impact: Builders can persist incompatible shapes and cannot prove cancellation or supersession validity during replay.
items.builder_discretion: All members, required evidence, reason codes, actors, timestamps, and cross-run references are open.

items.title: Planning Wizard disabled-state projection lacks GUI truth
items.statement: The Planning Wizard is named as a disabled-state consumer, but the contract does not map stored status, blockers, stale currentness, or missing receipts to visible state, reason ordering, actions, freshness, or recovery affordances.
items.impact: Different clients can show contradictory enabled states or omit the actionable reason PlanCompile is disabled.
items.builder_discretion: Projection inputs, precedence, copy or reason tokens, refresh behavior, and permitted user actions are open.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Resume by exact run id; stale currentness, unsupported contract mode, or missing receipts keep PlanCompile disabled.",

items.title: Redaction rules are descriptive, not enforceable
items.statement: The row promises ids, refs, hashes, stages, and enum status only, yet many fields are arbitrary strings or open objects and redaction_profile merely selects a label. No syntax, classifier, validator, or failure behavior prevents sensitive material from being embedded.
items.impact: Secrets or provider/account material can pass schema validation despite the no-secret rule.
items.builder_discretion: Sensitive-data detection, ref syntax, allowed hash/id formats, redaction transformation, and rejection or quarantine behavior are undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Stores ids, refs, hashes, stages, and enum status only; provider/account sensitive material remains external ref-only.",

items.title: Retention and compaction lack operational triggers
items.statement: Retention is expressed semantically, but there is no durable child/evidence completeness predicate, compaction trigger, deletion authority, tombstone behavior, or recovery rule.
items.impact: Implementations can retain indefinitely or compact too early, losing resumability or audit evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Lifecycle trigger, evaluator, grace period, deletion mechanics, historical indexing, and restoration behavior are open.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain through all child receipts and audit evidence; superseded runs are historical but not resumable unless currentness says so.",

items.title: Wave boundary arrays can be empty, duplicate, or conflicting
items.statement: read_set, write_set, forbidden_writes, and parent_only_writes are arrays of arbitrary strings with no minimum, uniqueness, normalization, disjointness, or precedence constraints, even though rows without boundaries are invalid for bootstrap.
items.impact: A wave can schema-validate with empty boundaries or with the same target simultaneously writable and forbidden, defeating isolation and parent-only ownership.
items.builder_discretion: Reference grammar, empty-set legality, overlap handling, glob semantics, path normalization, and precedence are undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Wave rows without read/write/forbidden boundaries are invalid for runtime bootstrap and remain source-lineage only.",

items.title: Wave result, completion receipt, and writeback invariants are missing
items.statement: result_status may be completed while completion_receipt remains null, and parent_writeback_required is an unconstrained boolean unrelated to parent_only_writes or result status. No conditional invariant establishes completion or writeback readiness.
items.impact: Parents and validators can accept a completed wave without durable completion evidence or skip required parent writeback.
items.builder_discretion: Completion evidence requirements, status-receipt coupling, writeback requirement derivation, and failure response are open.

items.title: Retry and resume semantics are not a state machine
items.statement: retry_route is any non-empty string and resume_ref is nullable, with no mapping from result status to retry eligibility, attempt identity, backoff, idempotency, supersession, or terminal failure.
items.impact: Failed or blocked waves can be retried inconsistently, duplicated, resumed from incompatible state, or loop forever.
items.builder_discretion: Retry routes, allowed transitions, maximum attempts, resume target grammar, idempotency key, and supersession rules are open.

items.title: No oracle enforces replay's product-work prohibition
items.statement: The contract states that replay must not dispatch product work but supplies no persisted replay mode, dispatch guard, event boundary, receipt assertion, or validation oracle that proves the prohibition held.
items.impact: A replay implementation can accidentally dispatch product work while still producing a schema-valid wave row.
items.builder_discretion: Replay detection, dispatch interception, side-effect accounting, failure behavior, and proof artifact are undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay restores assignment state and parent-only write obligations without dispatching product work.",

items.title: Agent role and producer names do not define authorization
items.statement: The producer is named and assigned_agent_role is persisted, but the role is any non-empty string and no principal identity, authorization check, delegation boundary, or signer binding governs who may allocate or complete a wave.
items.impact: Rows cannot prove that allocation, completion, or parent-write obligations came from an authorized actor.
items.builder_discretion: Role vocabulary, principal model, permission mapping, signature or receipt binding, and denial behavior are open.

items.title: Wave no-secret rule cannot reject secret-bearing strings
items.statement: The wave row promises document and PlanUnit references only, but all reference arrays and receipt fields accept arbitrary strings and redaction_profile is only an enum, so credentials or transcripts remain schema-valid.
items.impact: Sensitive provider material can be persisted in source refs, boundaries, evidence refs, or receipts despite the explicit prohibition.
items.builder_discretion: Allowed reference grammar, secret scanning, redaction method, validation point, and incident response are undefined.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Wave rows store document/PlanUnit refs and write boundaries only, never provider transcripts or credentials.",

items.title: Consumer propagation and parent writeback are not transactional
items.statement: Parent writeback, bootstrap validation, and evidence projection consume the row, but the contract does not define ordering, idempotency, atomicity, acknowledgement, partial-failure recovery, or how completion becomes visible across consumers.
items.impact: Consumers can observe contradictory result, evidence, and parent state or duplicate writeback after retry.
items.builder_discretion: Commit order, delivery mechanism, exactly-once or at-least-once semantics, deduplication key, and recovery are open.

items.title: No scale or performance bounds exist
items.statement: Cursor objects and all major reference, boundary, evidence, blocker, receipt, and artifact arrays lack maximum sizes, item-length limits, uniqueness, pagination, or compaction thresholds.
items.impact: Rows can grow without bound, harming redb transaction latency, memory use, replay time, and messagepack decode safety.
items.builder_discretion: Size caps, pagination, chunking, overflow behavior, deduplication, and compaction thresholds are open.

items.title: Migration outcomes lack a conversion and quarantine protocol
items.statement: Legacy PlanCompile drafts and invalid wave rows are relegated to non-buildable or source-lineage status, but no detection version, destination shape, conversion algorithm, quarantine location, error receipt, or reprocessing rule is defined.
items.impact: Migration tools can classify and preserve legacy data differently, making lineage and upgrade outcomes non-deterministic.
items.builder_discretion: Legacy detection, transformation, preservation location, diagnostics, retry, and audit evidence are open.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "No runtime PlanCompile rows are accepted without schema_version and contract_mode; old draft fields are imported only as non-buildable lineage.",
"migration": "Wave rows without read/write/forbidden boundaries are invalid for runtime bootstrap and remain source-lineage only.",

items.title: Canonical messagepack encoding is an undefined token
items.statement: Both families require messagepack_canonical, but the window provides no canonical map ordering, numeric/string normalization, extension handling, duplicate-key rule, or conformance vector.
items.impact: Independent encoders can produce different bytes and hashes for the same logical row, undermining deterministic receipts and replay.
items.builder_discretion: Canonicalization profile, library constraints, invalid-input behavior, and test vectors are open.

items.title: Timestamps lack ordering and mutation semantics
items.statement: created_at_utc and updated_at_utc are date-time strings, but no invariant requires creation at or before update, UTC normalization despite the field name, monotonic updates, or who may mutate timestamps.
items.impact: Replay ordering, freshness checks, and audit chronology can diverge or be forged while remaining schema-valid.
items.builder_discretion: Clock source, normalization, ordering, monotonicity, skew handling, and mutation authority are open.

dimension_assessments.summary: Replay intent is explicit for both families, but its gating and no-dispatch behaviors lack enforceable predicates and proofs.
The window establishes durable PlanCompile run state and compiler-wave assignment storage supporting resume, validation, projection, and parent writeback.
Keys and fields identify principal inputs and consumers, but key-to-payload binding and propagated output semantics are incomplete.
Top-level schemas are closed, but critical nested objects, cross-field invariants, write-boundary safety, and serialization canonicalization are unspecified.
Status enums exist without legal transition graphs, status-stage coupling, enablement transition, or retry/resume state machine.
Named producers and roles do not bind actions to principals, permissions, delegation, or signed receipts.
Both storage families name PNC-010 as owner documentation and explicitly name their producers.
Resume, GUI projection, readiness, parent writeback, validation, and evidence consumers are explicitly enumerated.
A Planning Wizard disabled-state projection is required, but its visible state mapping and recovery affordances are absent.
Fail-closed intent exists, but receipt completeness, retry routing, resume rules, and replay recovery are not deterministic.
No-secret prose is not enforced by reference grammars, secret validation, redaction mechanics, or authority binding.
Multiple consumers are identified without transaction ordering, idempotency, acknowledgement, or partial-failure semantics.
Retention intent and timestamps are present, but compaction triggers, chronology invariants, deletion authority, and recovery are absent.
Open objects and unbounded arrays have no size, pagination, chunking, or compaction limits.
Legacy exclusion rules are explicit, but conversion, quarantine, diagnostics, and reprocessing are not specified.
Structural schemas exist, but behavioral oracles for receipt completeness, safe replay, boundary conflicts, privacy, and writeback completion do not.
Consequential choices remain open across nested shapes, transitions, authority, GUI projection, boundaries, retries, retention, scaling, and encoding.
Staleness, receipt completeness, canonical encoding, runtime enablement, and migration outcomes have no exact operational definition in the authoritative core.
